analysis:
The PR adds provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCoreFoundation/OverlappedFileDigest.swift and calls it from WeightHasher.hashSingleFileUncached (WeightHasher.swift ~250-259). It replaces the serial 1 MiB read-then-hash loop with a dedicated pread thread that runs one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256, using two page-aligned buffers. The rest of the PR is docs (configuration.md, model-registry-format.md, a changelog) and tests.

I checked the replayed source for protocol and integrity problems.
- Digest integrity: SHA-256 is computed over the same bytes in file order, since the reader advances the offset by the bytes actually read. Short reads are handled.
- Semaphore handoff: free[0] and free[1] are signaled at start and filled starts at 0. The reader waits free[slot], does pread, stores lengths[slot], then signals filled[slot]. The caller waits filled[slot], hashes, then signals free[slot]. A buffer is never overwritten while the caller is hashing it. The reader stops on count <= 0.
- Error handling: a read error (count -1) yields nil, so the caller's existing fallback readers run. There is no partial digest. EISDIR and ESPIPE also return nil. The caller returns only after seeing count <= 0, which means the reader has already stopped, so the early return cannot deadlock.
- Use-after-close: `defer { readerExited.wait() }` ensures the reader thread has finished before the caller's close(descriptor) in hashSingleFileUncached. Buffers and lengths are freed in deinit after both threads are done.
- Semaphore deallocation: every semaphore has an initial value of 0 and never goes negative, so there is no libdispatch trap.
- Resource use: one extra thread and about 8 MiB of buffers per file being hashed, bounded by the existing worker concurrency. This does not materially affect availability (T-016, T-029).
- Threat model: weight-hash semantics (A-004, T-012, T-027) are unchanged, and the T-041 SSD cache pre/post-load hashes get the same digest. There is no new trust boundary, key handling, authorization or exposure. A file mutated during hashing behaves as before.
- Tests cover chunk boundaries, buffer wraparound and concurrent readers.

Residual limit: 18 replay units were omitted, but the changed source files appear fully in the replay. I found no security regression.
